third_place_rule: RANKING: The 12 third-placed teams are ranked by: (1) points in all group matches; (2) goal difference in all group matches; (3) goals scored in all group matches; (4) team conduct ("fair play") score (yellow card -1, indirect red/second yellow -3, direct red -4, yellow + direct red in same match -5, applied to players and team officials); (5) FIFA/Coca-Cola Men's World Ranking (most recent edition first). The top 8 advance to the Round of 32. ALLOCATION: There is no draw and no fixed "1st-best vs X" mapping. FIFA pre-published a lookup table in Annex C of the tournament regulations covering all C(12,8)=495 possible combinations of which 8 groups supply a qualifying third-placed team. For each combination, the table fixes which qualified third-placed team goes to which of the eight R32 slots (matches 74, 77, 79, 80, 81, 82, 85, 87). The mapping is constrained so that no team meets a team from its own group in the Round of 32 (each group winner's slot only admits third-placed teams from 5 specific other groups, as encoded in the away_source fields: M74 Winner E vs 3rd A/B/C/D/F; M77 Winner I vs 3rd C/D/F/G/H; M79 Winner A vs 3rd C/E/F/H/I; M80 Winner L vs 3rd E/H/I/J/K; M81 Winner D vs 3rd B/E/F/I/J; M82 Winner G vs 3rd A/E/H/I/J; M85 Winner B vs 3rd E/F/G/I/J; M87 Winner K vs 3rd D/E/I/J/L). Once the eight qualifiers are known after the final group matches, the corresponding Annex C row locks the bracket automatically; for simulation purposes the row-level table (495 rows) must be taken from FIFA Regulations Annex C (also reproduced as a table on the Wikipedia knockout-stage article).
tiebreaker_rules: Teams ranked in groups by points (win 3, draw 1, loss 0). If two or more teams are equal on points, the order is: (1) most points in group matches between the teams concerned (head-to-head); (2) goal difference in matches between the teams concerned; (3) goals scored in matches between the teams concerned; (4) goal difference in ALL group matches; (5) goals scored in ALL group matches; (6) highest team conduct ("fair play") score in all group matches (yellow card -1, indirect red card/second yellow -3, direct red card -4, yellow card plus direct red card in same match -5; counted for players and team officials); (7) FIFA/Coca-Cola Men's World Ranking (most recently published edition first, earlier editions sequentially if still tied). Note: head-to-head comes BEFORE overall goal difference at the 2026 edition, and there is no drawing of lots (replaced by FIFA ranking). Cross-checked across ESPN, worldcuplocaltime and FIFA-derived summaries.
caveats: 1) Dates are local (venue) dates per Wikipedia; Sky Sports lists UK kick-off times, which push three late-evening games (matches 92, 94, 100) to the next calendar day in UK time — I used local dates (92: 07-05, 94: 07-06, 100: 07-11). All match pairings are identical across both sources. 2) home_source/away_source ordering follows the official schedule listing; the "home" designation is nominal. 3) The full 495-row Annex C combination table (exact slot assignment for every possible set of 8 qualifying third-place groups) exists on the Wikipedia knockout-stage page and in FIFA Regulations Annex C but is too large to reproduce here; only the per-slot allowed-group constraints (5 groups per slot, verified internally consistent: 8 slots x 5 = 40 appearances, no same-group winner/3rd pairing) are encoded above. A simulator that needs exact deterministic slotting (not just the allowed-group sets) must ingest that table separately. 4) FIFA.com pages (knockout bracket article, tie-breakers article) did not render via fetch (JS-only), so FIFA primary-source text was obtained via secondary outlets quoting the regulations; the regulations PDF itself was not fetched. 5) Bracket-side/path constraints for third-placed teams beyond the allowed-group lists (e.g. which combination row applies) are deterministic per Annex C, not drawn.
